original_answer:
**Effectiveness period:** A new series of an existing trust filed under Rule 485(a) generally becomes effective on the **75th day after filing**, absent a delaying amendment or earlier staff action. Rule 485(b) can make an amendment effective sooner, but it is generally unavailable for a new series without a qualifying basis. A Rule 6c-11 ETF needs no exemptive order, so 485(a) applies.

**Why it isn't a launch guarantee:** Effectiveness only makes the series legally registered. Launch still depends on:
- Exchange listing approval and ticker or CUSIP assignment
- Seed capital and authorized participant agreements
- Custody, transfer agent, and fund accounting setup
- Blue-sky notice filings and NSCC/DTC readiness
- Staff comments that may require a further amendment, which can push the date back

**Initial registration of a new trust:** A brand-new trust files a Form N-1A registration statement under Section 8(a) and Rule 485(a) and typically also faces the 75-day period. The trust must first be formed under state law and register under the Investment Company Act, which adds steps before any series can launch.
